questions.question: Define natural resources and explain the difference between renewable and non-renewable resources.
questions.expected_answer: Natural resources: things in nature people use for food, water, shelter, energy, raw materials; depend on knowledge and technology (uranium, solar). Unevenly distributed; SA rich in minerals (PGMs, manganese, chromium, gold, coal, iron ore, diamonds), water scarce (about 450 mm rain). Non-renewable: fixed amount or forms too slowly; used up. Renewable: replaced by natural processes within a human lifetime or always available.

questions.question: Describe non-renewable resources, using South African examples.
questions.expected_answer: Fossil fuels: coal, oil, gas from ancient plants and sea creatures; SA coal 250-300 million years old (Mpumalanga, Limpopo); around 80% of electricity, Sasol fuels from coal at Secunda; CO2 and air pollution; little oil, imported. Minerals: gold, platinum, iron ore, diamonds; ore deposits finite even if metals recycled; gold peaked 1970 (about 1 000 t), mines over 3 km deep. Use efficiently, recycle, find alternatives.

questions.question: Describe renewable resources and explain why all resources must be used wisely.
questions.expected_answer: Flow/inexhaustible: sunlight, wind, tides; SA high solar radiation (Northern Cape), coastal wind; REIPPPP since 2011, rooftop solar. Conditionally renewable: water, soil, forests, grasslands, fish; renew only within sustainable yield; overuse (overfishing, deforestation, erosion, groundwater overpumping) can destroy them. Wise use: population growth (2.5 billion 1950 to over 8 billion), benefits (jobs, exports) vs costs (pollution, acid mine drainage, climate change, declining mining towns); energy transition and just transition for Mpumalanga coal communities.
